results.name: Basic Event Stream
results.description: Credential for EventStreams that use Basic Authentication. It requires a username and password

fields.label: Username
fields.help_text: The username used to authenticate the incoming event stream

fields.label: Password
fields.help_text: The password used to authenticate the incoming event stream

results.name: Dynatrace Event Stream
results.description: Credential for Dynatrace Event Stream. This is a clone of the Basic authentication.

fields.label: Username
fields.help_text: The username used to authenticate the incoming event stream

fields.label: Password
fields.help_text: The password used to authenticate the incoming event stream

fields.label: HTTP Header Key
fields.help_text: The HTTP header for passing in the credentials usually this is Authorization.

results.name: ECDSA Event Stream
results.description: Credential for Event Streams that use Elliptic Curve DSA. This requires a public key and the headers that carry the signature.

fields.label: Primary Header Key
fields.help_text: The sender will use this HTTP header to pass in the signature

fields.label: Public Key
fields.help_text: Public Key for validating the data, this would be available from the sender after you have created the event stream on their side with our URL. This is usually a 2 step process

fields.label: Additional Prefix Header Key
fields.help_text: Additional Header Key for ECDSA.

fields.label: Signature Encoding
fields.help_text: The payload signature which is binary is converted as a base64 or hex strings before being added to the HTTP header

fields.label: Hash algorithm
fields.help_text: The EventStream sender hashes the message being sent using one of these algorithms, which guarantees message integrity.

results.name: GitHub Event Stream
results.description: Credential for Github EventStream. This is a specialization of the HMAC authentication which only requires a secret to be provided.

fields.label: HMAC Secret
fields.help_text: The symmetrical shared secret between EDA and the EventStream Server. Please save this value since you would need it on the EventStream Server.

fields.label: HMAC Algorithm
fields.help_text: The EventStream sender hashes the message being sent using one of these algorithms, which guarantees message integrity.

fields.label: HTTP Header Key
fields.help_text: The event stream sender typically uses a special HTTP header to send the signature of the payload. e.g X-Hub-Signature-256

fields.label: Signature Encoding
fields.help_text: The payload signature which is binary is converted as a base64 or hex strings before being added to the HTTP header

fields.label: Signature prefix
fields.help_text: The signature might optionally have a prefix.e.g sha256=

results.name: GitLab Event Stream
results.description: Credential for Gitlab Event Streams. This is a specialization of the Token authentication with the X-Gitlab-Token header.

fields.label: Token
fields.help_text: The symmetrical shared token between EDA and the Gitlab Server. Please save this value since you would need it on the EventStream Server.

fields.label: HTTP Header Key
fields.help_text: The HTTP header for passing in the token usually this is Authorization but some sites use a different header, e.g. X-Gitlab-Token

results.name: HMAC Event Stream
results.description: Credential for Event Streams that use HMAC. This requires shared secret between the sender and receiver. The signature can be sent as hex or base64 strings. Most of senders will use a special HTTP header to send the signature data.

fields.label: Secret
fields.help_text: The symmetrical shared secret between EDA and the Event Stream Server. Please save this value since you would need it on the Event Stream Server.

fields.label: Hash algorithm
fields.help_text: The EventStream sender hashes the message being sent using one of these algorithms, which guarantees message integrity.

fields.label: HMAC Header Key
fields.help_text: The event stream sender typically uses a special HTTP header to send the signature of the payload. e.g X-Hub-Signature-256

fields.label: Signature Encoding
fields.help_text: The payload signature which is binary is converted as a base64 or hex strings before being added to the HTTP header

fields.label: Signature prefix
fields.help_text: The signature might optionally have a prefix.e.g sha256=

results.name: mTLS Event Stream
results.description: Credential for Event Streams that use mutual TLS. The Certificate is installed in the Web Server and we can optionally validate the Subject defined in the Certificate.

fields.label: Certificate Subject
fields.help_text: The Subject from Certificate compliant with RFC 2253.This is optional and can be used to check the subject defined in the certificate.

fields.label: HTTP Header Key
fields.help_text: The NGINX Server passes the certificate subject using this HTTP header

results.name: OAuth2 Event Stream
results.description: Credential for Event Streams that use OAuth2. This needs a client id and client credential and access to an Authorization server so we can introspect the token being sent.

fields.label: Client ID
fields.help_text: The Client ID from the Authorization Server.

fields.label: Client Secret
fields.help_text: The Client Secret from the Authorization Server.

fields.label: Introspection URL
fields.help_text: The Introspection URL from the Authorization Server as defined in RFC 7662.

fields.label: HTTP Header Key
fields.help_text: The HTTP header for passing in the token usually this is Authorization.

results.name: OAuth2 JWT Event Stream
results.description: Credential for Event Streams that use OAuth2 with JWT. This needs a JWKS URL which will be used to fetch the public key and validate the incoming token. If an audience is specified we will check the audience in the JWT claims.

fields.label: JWKS URL
fields.help_text: JSON Web Key Sets URL to fetch public keys to validate JWT token. Its usually https://<your auth server>/.well-known/jwks.json

fields.label: Audience
fields.help_text: Audience from the JWT claims, if specified we will validate the audience in the JWT claims.

fields.label: HTTP Header Key
fields.help_text: The HTTP header for passing in the token usually this is Authorization.

results.name: ServiceNow Event Stream
results.description: Credential for ServiceNow Event Stream. This is a specialization of the Token authentication which only requires a token to be provided.

fields.label: Token
fields.help_text: The symmetrical shared token between EDA and the ServiceNow Server. Please save this value since you would need it on the EventStream Server.

fields.label: HTTP Header Key
fields.help_text: The HTTP header for passing in the token usually this is Authorization but some sites use a different header, e.g. X-Gitlab-Token
